solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Defender having a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist of an argument is its point

explanation.surface: A defender in some sport is credited with a game point.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist argues in defence of a cause or belief, so is its defender.

clue.text: Recover spirits when incidental benefit has increased

parts.note: a perk is a fringe benefit of a job
up means risen or increased

explanation.surface: Morale recovers once the job's extra benefit has gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To perk up is to become more cheerful, recovering one's spirits.

clue.text: Fielder taking considerable time in advance

parts.note: long means a considerable time
on means forward or ahead, as in getting on

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder takes ages getting into position early.
explanation.walkthrough: LONG ON is a cricket fielding position deep behind the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, long on names both the deep position and the player fielding there.

clue.text: Lady from Rutherglen dancing

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the name is drawn from the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A woman from Rutherglen, a town near Glasgow, takes to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Glenda is a woman's first name, so it gives one particular lady.

clue.text: Make a difference?

parts.note: making a difference usually means having an effect, but a difference is also a quarrel, and making one means picking a fight

explanation.definitionFit: A difference of opinion is a dispute, so creating one means beginning a row.

clue.text: Star we're looking forward to seeing

definitions.meaning: the star item is the outstanding feature of an event
the best part of a show, the moment the audience most anticipates

explanation.definitionFit: A highlight is the outstanding or most memorable part, the star attraction everyone anticipates.

clue.text: No government advocate

parts.note: reads as someone who works for no state department, but means a person who argues for having no government at all

explanation.definitionFit: Anarchists favour abolishing the state, campaigning for society without rulers.

clue.text: Attend one duet performed with extreme happiness

parts.note: to be at an event is to attend it
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a performed piece is worked over, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes to watch a duet and is overjoyed by the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' rearranges DUET into TUDE; 'with' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude means supreme blessedness, a state of utmost bliss.

clue.text: Doubles partner in cafe upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player's doubles partner is in a café, feeling upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges IN and CAFE. 'Doubles partner' suggests tennis, but it is someone you are pairing up with for life.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed person is the partner one is about to double up with in marriage, a playful sense of doubles.

clue.text: Protestant, a German on manoeuvres!

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters before it are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A Protestant exclaims at a German soldier out on military manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges A GERMAN ON. An Orangeman belongs to the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal society in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order are by definition Protestants, so an Orangeman is an example of one.

clue.text: Half number by the way having ardent desire

indicators.note: half of a word means only its first four of eight letters are kept here

parts.note: thirteen is a number
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone halfway along a street is consumed by passionate longing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps THIR, the first half of THIRTEEN; 'by' sets ST beside it, and 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is used figuratively for a strong craving, as in a thirst for knowledge.

clue.text: Too old for an appointment?

definitions.meaning: past its time, no longer current
a cryptic reading: out (on a) date, away to meet a date

explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated is too old to be current, and someone out on a date is off for a romantic appointment.

clue.text: One over there includes one new helmet

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the first piece wraps around the others

parts.note: that points to one over there, as opposed to this
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A distant figure is wearing a fresh helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin hat is slang for a soldier's steel helmet, especially from the World Wars.

clue.text: Next to notice Joseph at home in middle of night

parts.note: an ad is a notice, as in a newspaper advertisement
Jo is a short form of the name Joseph
in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: middle of means only the central letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A note is pinned up telling Joseph to be home by midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is taken as written, sitting between IN for 'at home' and G, the central letter of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjoining describes things side by side, abutting each other, so means beside.

clue.text: Dumpy one's new name

indicators.note: new suggests making something fresh, so these letters are shaped into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A short, plump person has been given a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DUMPYONES, the letters of 'Dumpy one's', including the S of the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a false or pen name, adopted in place of one's real one.

clue.text: Page inserted to cover part of foliage

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth
a leaf is one part of a plant's foliage

explanation.surface: A page is slipped in to hide a bit of greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: An interleaf is an extra blank sheet bound between the regular pages of a book.

clue.text: Object achieved at last

definitions.meaning: an object is an aim or goal
something achieved at last comes in the finish, at the close

explanation.definitionFit: An end is a purpose one aims at, and 'in the end' describes what comes at last.

clue.text: Did not start at this place earlier

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word for the place goes

parts.note: here means at this place

explanation.surface: Someone failed to begin at this spot before.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is an old word meaning before, so it gives earlier in a poetic register.

clue.text: Acid also taken up

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means read from bottom to top, so the word turns around

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone has started taking acid too.
explanation.definitionFit: DNA, deoxyribonucleic acid, is the nucleic acid carrying genetic information.

clue.text: Not able to make one's mark at the election

definitions.text: Not able to make one's mark at the election

parts.words: Not able to make one's mark at the election
parts.note: making one's mark suggests achieving fame, but here it is putting a cross on a ballot paper, which someone without a vote cannot do

explanation.definitionFit: To be deprived of the vote is to be unable to mark a ballot paper in an election.

clue.text: Be hesitant a very long time

parts.note: er is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Someone takes a very long time to make up their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long historical period, a very lengthy span of time.

clue.text: Compositions spouse rubbished

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed, so the letters of the word before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A husband or wife sneered at someone's musical works.
explanation.definitionFit: Opuses are musical or literary works, each numbered composition being an opus.

clue.text: In shop Tim accepted most favourable points

indicators.note: in means contained inside, so the answer lies within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: Tim was taken on in a shop at its busiest times.
explanation.definitionFit: Optima is the plural of optimum, the best or most favourable point or condition.

clue.text: Support a Scottish island

parts.note: a staff is a stick used for support

explanation.surface: Someone backs a particular island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffa is an island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small uninhabited island off the west coast of Mull in Scotland.

clue.text: Official residence father started leaving before one

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: started means only the start, the first letter, of the word after it is used

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Dad set off from home ahead of one other person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link placing the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence of a monarch, bishop or head of state.

clue.text: Hind's piece of meat

parts.note: a hind is a female deer, but read as hind quarters it points to a cut taken from a beast's backside

explanation.definitionFit: This cut of beef comes from the rump, the hind part of the animal.

clue.text: One old reformed simpleton

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the two words before it are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly person has turned over a new leaf and become a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal for a silly or foolish person, literally a head with nothing in it.

clue.text: Chart of Mafeking?

parts.note: the Relief of Mafeking was a famous Boer War episode, so a chart of it would playfully be a chart of the relief; really it is a map showing hills

explanation.walkthrough: Mafeking, a South African town, was besieged in the Boer War and its 1900 relief was celebrated wildly in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows the heights and contours of terrain, a type of chart.

clue.text: Two Poles with agreement to contradict

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles, and each takes AY, an old word of agreement
N and S are the north and south poles, and each takes AY, an old word of agreement

explanation.surface: Two Polish people come to an understanding about disagreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: Each pole gets its own AY: N with AY, then S with AY.
explanation.definitionFit: To naysay is to deny or oppose, speaking against what someone else says.

clue.text: Plan to put stone by layers of rock

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A scheme to place a stone on top of rock layers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or scheme to outwit someone.
